pages.quiz:
CREATIVE ARTS — MOCK EXAM #12
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: CREATIVE ARTS
TIME ALLOWED: 90 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 80
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. What is the job of the hollow shell of a drum? (1 mark)
   A. To hold the beater
   B. To tie the ropes
   C. To make the sound fuller and louder
   D. To keep the skin wet

2. Who must do the burning when making charcoal sticks? (1 mark)
   A. An adult or the teacher
   B. The youngest learner
   C. Any learner
   D. Nobody

3. A melodic percussion instrument is one that (1 mark)
   A. has no parts
   B. can play different notes to make a tune
   C. is always loud
   D. can only make one sound

4. Which of these is a percussion instrument? (1 mark)
   A. Whistle
   B. Recorder
   C. Drum
   D. Trumpet

5. In a double-handed catch, where should your eyes be? (1 mark)
   A. On the ground
   B. On the ball until it is in your hands
   C. On the next player
   D. On the crowd

6. A player who catches the ball must not (1 mark)
   A. throw it to a teammate
   B. pivot on the landing foot
   C. run with it
   D. pass it

7. Which of these is a light tone of purple? (1 mark)
   A. Pure purple
   B. Purple mixed with black
   C. Purple mixed with white
   D. Purple mixed with brown

8. How many secondary colours are there on the basic colour wheel? (1 mark)
   A. Three
   B. Six
   C. Two
   D. Nine

9. A rest is a sign for (1 mark)
   A. silence
   B. the loudest sound
   C. a repeat
   D. a song title

10. How long does one quaver last? (1 mark)
   A. Two beats
   B. Half a beat
   C. A quarter of a beat only
   D. One beat

11. The line on which letters sit is called the (1 mark)
   A. baseline
   B. descender line
   C. border
   D. ascender line

12. How long does a quaver rest last? (1 mark)
   A. Half a beat
   B. One beat
   C. Four beats
   D. Two beats

13. How many rectangular slabs of different sizes are cut in this lesson? (1 mark)
   A. Three
   B. Five
   C. Ten
   D. One

14. Which move is a step? (1 mark)
   A. d to r
   B. m to d in one jump over r
   C. d to d
   D. d to m

15. Which is the lowest of the notes d, r and m? (1 mark)
   A. They are all the same
   B. d
   C. m
   D. r

16. In the worked melody of this lesson, the last note is (1 mark)
   A. a pair of quavers
   B. m, a quaver
   C. d, a crotchet
   D. r, a rest

17. The Kenyan flag has stripes of (1 mark)
   A. blue, yellow and white
   B. black, red and green with thin white stripes
   C. orange and green
   D. red, white and blue

18. On the Kenyan flag, white stands for (1 mark)
   A. the people
   B. the sky
   C. peace and honesty
   D. blood

19. At the set position, the hips are (1 mark)
   A. a little higher than the shoulders
   B. lower than the knees
   C. behind the line only
   D. on the ground

20. In a crab balance, your body is supported by (1 mark)
   A. the head only
   B. the back only
   C. the knees and elbows
   D. both hands and both feet

21. A good sequence has (1 mark)
   A. only noise
   B. no order
   C. only jumps
   D. a clear start, smooth middle and controlled finish

22. A sign that gets wider to the right means (1 mark)
   A. getting softer
   B. getting louder
   C. stop
   D. slow

23. When singing, you should breathe (1 mark)
   A. deeply so your tummy moves out gently
   B. by shouting
   C. by holding your breath
   D. only through the ears

24. The centre of interest is (1 mark)
   A. the main thing you want people to notice
   B. the middle of the room
   C. the edge of the photo
   D. the camera button

25. The word photography comes from words meaning (1 mark)
   A. drawing with sound
   B. drawing with paint
   C. drawing with light
   D. writing with ink

26. Tonguing means (1 mark)
   A. saying too or doo quietly at the start of each note
   B. singing loudly
   C. chewing
   D. rolling on the floor

27. In water tag, players (1 mark)
   A. run on the pool side
   B. walk fast, not run, and tag gently
   C. hold others under water
   D. push others

28. In the giraffe stretch, you (1 mark)
   A. stand tall on toes with arms high
   B. crawl
   C. swim
   D. roll

29. Animal games improve (1 mark)
   A. only reading
   B. only cooking
   C. only singing
   D. fitness and health

30. Good feedback should be (1 mark)
   A. only criticism
   B. rude and short
   C. only praise with no reasons
   D. kind, honest, specific and helpful

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
31. Why is it important to appreciate the works of people from different cultures? (3 marks)

32. Describe how to make a ball using the macramé technique and overhand knots. (5 marks)

33. Why do we scratch and wet clay before joining pieces? (3 marks)

34. State the role of the Kenya National Anthem. (3 marks)

35. Why is it good to take different roles in animal games? (3 marks)

36. Describe how to do the crab walk and name the muscles it strengthens. (3 marks)

37. Explain what overlapping is and why it is used in a montage. (3 marks)

38. What is a side roll? (2 marks)

39. Describe the position of the back knee in the medium start and in the elongated start. (3 marks)

40. State four performance techniques for a good singer. (4 marks)

41. Describe the sit-and-slide water entry. (3 marks)

42. Give four hygiene measures for using a recorder. (4 marks)

43. Name two digital devices used for taking photographs. (2 marks)

44. Describe the correct posture and hand position for playing the recorder. (4 marks)

45. Describe a sequence that joins the crab balance and the side roll, and how to perform it safely. (5 marks)
pages.answers:
CREATIVE ARTS — MOCK EXAM #12 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. C — To make the sound fuller and louder
   The air inside the hollow body makes the sound louder.

2. A — An adult or the teacher
   Fire is dangerous, so only an adult does the burning.

3. B — can play different notes to make a tune
   Melodic instruments such as the xylophone play notes of different pitch.

4. C — Drum
   A drum is struck to make sound. The others are played by blowing.

5. B — On the ball until it is in your hands
   Watching the ball helps you catch it.

6. C — run with it
   Running with the ball is against the rules.

7. C — Purple mixed with white
   White makes a tint.

8. A — Three
   Orange, green and purple are the three secondary colours.

9. A — silence
   A rest tells the performer to stay silent for a time.

10. B — Half a beat
   A quaver is half a beat.

11. A — baseline
   All letters sit on the baseline.

12. A — Half a beat
   A quaver rest is half a beat of silence.

13. A — Three
   Three slabs are cut, one for each of d, r and m.

14. A — d to r
   Doh to ray is to the next note.

15. B — d
   Doh is the lowest of the three.

16. C — d, a crotchet
   The final note is d, on a crotchet.

17. B — black, red and green with thin white stripes
   The flag has black, red, green and white.

18. C — peace and honesty
   White stands for peace and honesty.

19. A — a little higher than the shoulders
   On set the hips lift slightly above the shoulders.

20. D — both hands and both feet
   A crab balance rests on two hands and two feet.

21. D — a clear start, smooth middle and controlled finish
   Good sequences are planned and controlled.

22. B — getting louder
   An opening sign means the music grows louder.

23. A — deeply so your tummy moves out gently
   Deep breathing supports the voice.

24. A — the main thing you want people to notice
   It draws the eye first.

25. C — drawing with light
   Photography means drawing with light.

26. A — saying too or doo quietly at the start of each note
   Tonguing separates notes clearly.

27. B — walk fast, not run, and tag gently
   No pushing.

28. A — stand tall on toes with arms high
   Reach up like a giraffe.

29. D — fitness and health
   They strengthen muscles and improve stamina.

30. D — kind, honest, specific and helpful
   Good feedback helps the person improve.

SECTION B
----
31. (3 marks)
   Answer: We learn about others, it builds respect and unity and it helps us value all cultures.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

32. (5 marks)
   Answer: Make a firm core from paper or cloth. Cut equal cords. Tie them together with an overhand knot at the middle. Put the core on top. Tie overhand knots between pairs of neighbouring cords to make a net around the core. Gather the cords at the bottom and tie a strong knot.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each of five clear stages.

33. (3 marks)
   Answer: It makes the surface rough and sticky so the pieces hold together and do not fall off when dry.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for scratching, 1 mark for water, 1 mark for the reason.

34. (3 marks)
   Answer: It is a national symbol that unites Kenyans, shows love for the country and reminds us of our values.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

35. (3 marks)
   Answer: Everyone gets a fair turn, learns to lead and follow, and the team works better.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

36. (3 marks)
   Answer: Sit, put hands behind, lift the hips and walk on hands and feet with tummy up. It strengthens the arms, shoulders and tummy.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the position, 1 mark for walking, 1 mark for muscles.

37. (3 marks)
   Answer: Overlapping means placing one piece so it partly covers another. It removes gaps and makes the montage look full and joined up.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the meaning, 2 marks for the reasons.

38. (2 marks)
   Answer: A roll along the mat sideways with the body straight and long like a log.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for sideways roll, 1 mark for the straight body.

39. (3 marks)
   Answer: In the medium start, the back knee is level with the middle of the front foot. In the elongated start it is level with the heel of the front foot.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each position, 1 mark for saying the elongated start is further back.

40. (4 marks)
   Answer: Good posture; deep breathing; clear diction; gestures; facial expression; eye contact. Any four.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

41. (3 marks)
   Answer: Sit on the edge with feet in the water, hands on the edge beside the hips. Turn to face the wall and slide gently into the water holding the edge.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each part.

42. (4 marks)
   Answer: Wash hands before playing; do not share it without cleaning; do not eat while playing; wipe the mouthpiece; clean it properly. Any four.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

43. (2 marks)
   Answer: Smartphone, tablet, digital camera. Any two.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

44. (4 marks)
   Answer: Sit or stand tall. Hold the recorder pointing down and away. The left hand is at the top and the right hand at the bottom. The left thumb covers the thumb hole and fingers cover holes with the pads.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

45. (5 marks)
   Answer: Warm up and use a mat with a clear space. Do a crab balance and hold for three counts. Lower to the mat and lie straight with arms overhead. Do a side roll in a straight line. Get up slowly and finish standing tall.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each for safety, crab balance, lowering, roll, and finish.
